findings.title: KeyError when reinstalling integrations without sender in metadata
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch()`, the code accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` to compare with the authenticated GitHub user. However, integrations created before this change may not have a `"sender"` key in their metadata (it is only set in `build_integration` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy). When such an existing active integration is encountered (e.g., during a reinstall flow), this line will raise `KeyError`, producing a 500 error for the user instead of the intended graceful error page. The access should use `.get()` with a safe default, e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`.

findings.title: Uncaught exceptions in get_user_info will produce 500 errors
findings.body: After exchanging the OAuth code, the view calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` without any exception handling. If this call fails due to a network error, timeout, invalid token, or any other error, the exception will propagate up and result in a 500 error instead of the intended graceful error page. The view already catches broad exceptions when parsing the token response, so a similar try/except around `get_user_info` (and around `safe_urlopen` itself) is needed to ensure all failure paths return the `error()` page like the other validation failures do.

findings.title: No timeout on OAuth token exchange request
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is called without a timeout argument. If the GitHub OAuth endpoint hangs or is slow, this view will block indefinitely. Given the other `safe_urlopen` callers in the codebase typically pass an explicit `timeout=`, this call should do the same to avoid tying up worker threads on a hung OAuth handshake.

findings.title: OAuth token exchange does not send redirect_uri or Accept header
findings.body: The token exchange POST to GitHub sends `code`, `client_id`, and `client_secret` but omits the `redirect_uri` and an `Accept: application/json` header. While GitHub is usually lenient about `redirect_uri`, many OAuth client configurations require it to exactly match the value used at the authorize step, and on failure GitHub returns the error body as JSON (which `parse_qsl` will misparse, leading to the generic "access_token not in payload" path instead of logging the real `error_description`). Both `redirect_uri` and `Accept` should be included for correctness and debuggability.

findings.title: test_github_user_mismatch uses hardcoded state and may pass for wrong reason
findings.body: `test_github_user_mismatch` builds `setup_path_2` with the hardcoded state `"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"` (the same value asserted in `assert_setup_flow`). It then logs in as a different user (`user_2`) in a different org (`org_2`) before issuing the GETs. If `pipeline.signature` depends on the user or organization, this state will not match the pipeline started by `user_2/org_2`, and the test will pass due to state mismatch — not user mismatch. The assertion only checks for the generic `"Invalid installation request."` string, which is the same error returned for state mismatch, so the test does not actually verify the user-mismatch code path. The test should extract the actual `state` from the redirect URL returned by `init_path_2` (or otherwise obtain the correct signature) and use that in `setup_path_2`, and ideally assert a more specific error indicator.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found behavior
findings.body: `test_installation_not_found` stubs a 404 for `/app/installations/{installation_id}` and then calls the setup path with `installation_id` and again with `code` + `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"` (which deliberately does not match any pipeline signature). The first GET just bounces through `OAuthLoginView` to GitHub authorize; the second GET fails at the state check before ever reaching `build_integration`, so the 404 stub is never exercised. The test now only verifies that the generic "Invalid installation request." error is shown — the same error shown for state mismatch. Either the test should be renamed to reflect what it actually verifies, or it should be rewritten to complete the OAuth step (with a correct state) so that `build_integration` is reached and the 404 path in `get_installation_info` is actually tested.
